data.title: ICESCO, UNESCO Hold International Symposium on Islamic Art
data.content:
Rabat, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The Islamic World Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (ICESCO) and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) held a virtual international symposium today to mark the International Day of Islamic Art. The symposium, titled "Islamic Art: A Precious Heritage and Contemporary Challenges to Its Preservation," brought together officials from international organizations, academics, and experts in Islamic art and heritage.
    ICESCO Director-General Dr. Salim M. AlMalik highlighted the importance of digital documentation in protecting at-risk heritage and making it accessible to the public. He also pointed to the role of the International Fair and Museum of the Prophet's Biography and Islamic Civilization at ICESCO headquarters in Rabat in familiarizing visitors with Islamic cultural heritage.
    Discussions focused on the cultural and historical significance of Islamic art, digital preservation, and support for young artists and artisans. Participants also discussed passing traditional skills to future generations, protecting historic landmarks, and preserving the craftsmanship involved in their construction.
    -- SPA
